capabilities.name: Turn serialization and per-session runtime state (lease, run generations, slot claim, concurrency cap, stale/reaped eviction, warm agent cache)
capabilities.hermes: A turn lease serializes `[load history → run → flush]` per resolved session id (not per routing key). Run generations let a late callback from an abandoned turn detect it no longer owns the session. An active-session slot is claimed before any await, bounded by `max_concurrent_sessions`. Watchdogs evict a session that still claims a running agent but made no progress, and one whose durable routing row was ended while the in-memory slot stayed alive. One `SessionState` object holds all per-session state with three explicit lifetimes; a per-session warm `AIAgent` cache preserves the prompt prefix and is evicted under cgroup memory pressure. ~14 entries incl. gw-core.turn-lease / run-generation / session-slot-claim / agent-cache / agent-cache-pressure / contextvar-reset.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: agents/core/orchestrator.py:594,1164 uses an `_active_session` ContextVar so a per-request session binding cannot clobber a concurrent turn — that is the leak guard and it is correct (tests/test_concurrent_session_isolation.py). Missing: no lease, no generation counter, no slot claim, no `max_concurrent_sessions`, no stale-turn eviction, no warm-agent cache. `rg 'max_concurrent|turn_lease' agents/` finds only the unrelated company-mode `max_concurrent`.
capabilities.rationale: Nerva solved the easier half (don't let two turns see each other's identity) and skipped the harder half (don't let two turns run at once). A hub that also drives cameras, the house and a company-mode work run needs a hard cap on simultaneous agent turns or a message burst becomes a resource incident on the owner's own box. The lease is also the precondition for row 4's busy semantics.
capabilities.governance: Read-only with respect to the world; but the concurrency cap is a real safety bound — it limits how many kernel-mediated actions can be in flight at once, which the budget layer (agents/core/kernel/budget.py) currently bounds by spend rather than by parallelism.

capabilities.rationale: Hermes's Ralph loop is an unbounded continuation with a judge; Nerva's is a budgeted, approved, night-aware work run whose every step re-crosses the kernel. Keeping it is not conservatism — it is the whole thesis. What to copy is only the doorway: a chat verb that proposes a goal, and `/subgoal`-style mid-run criteria (Nerva's goal_contract can hold them but nothing lets the owner add one from a phone). `/review` is worth copying as a chat entry point to the existing reviewer path.
capabilities.governance: `goal.approve` — already registered and kernel-mediated. A chat verb must enqueue a decision card, never start a run directly.

capabilities.name: User-defined quick commands (`/x` → shell exec or alias)
capabilities.hermes: `quick_commands:` in config maps a short slash name to `{type: exec, command: systemctl status hermes-agent}` or `{type: alias, target: /gmail unread}`. Exec runs `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell` in the gateway process with a sanitised env (`build_subprocess_env()`), a 30 s timeout, and output passed through `redact_sensitive_text`. Alias rewrites the message text and re-resolves. Built-ins always win, and slash-access is re-checked on the raw typed name. 2 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: none. The nearest thing Nerva has is the governed path: agents/core/kernel/registry.py `terminal.exec` ("a durable accepted task is required before any process exists, and the irreversible tier keeps this at the approval QUEUE floor"), agents/core/environments/execution.py, and the `JARVIS_TERMINAL_TARGETS` / `JARVIS_TERMINAL_LOCAL_HOST` flags in docs/FLAGS.md:346,350.
capabilities.rationale: The alias half is pure ergonomics and should be copied as-is. The exec half is the single sharpest adaptation in this cluster: Hermes runs arbitrary shell as the gateway user from a chat message, guarded only by a 30 s timeout and an env scrub. In Nerva the same feature must be a named, pre-registered command whose execution is a `terminal.exec` task — hardline denylist, target policy, durable approval, contract, kernel GRANT — so a ported convenience does not become the one unmediated way to run code on the owner's box. Ported that way it is still worth having: it is the shortest path from 'I need to check the NAS' to a governed, audited one-liner.
capabilities.governance: `terminal.exec` — irreversible tier, approval-queue floor, requires JARVIS_ACTION_KERNEL. Never `create_subprocess_shell` from a command handler.

capabilities.name: Plugin- and skill-registered commands, bundles, stacked skills, and command discovery (`/help`, `/commands`, `/bundles`)
capabilities.hermes: A plugin owns a `/name` on every chat platform via `register_command`, discovered lazily so plugin import never happens at startup, with underscore→hyphen normalisation at lookup and arg-required third-party commands excluded from Telegram's menu. `/<skill-name>` injects the whole SKILL.md body into the next user turn; up to 5 skills can be stacked (`/a /b do XYZ`); `/<bundle-slug>` loads several skills at once; skills whose slug collides with a core command are refused registration and logged. `/help`, `/commands` (paginated over commands and skills) and `/bundles` are the discovery surface. ~11 entries.

Copy the registration API and the collision rule — 'a skill may never shadow a core command' is a small rule that prevents a supply-chain-shaped problem, given that a skill is code the owner installed from a marketplace. Discovery (`/help`, `/commands`) is the floor row 2 already assumes exists.

capabilities.name: Lifecycle hooks (`pre_command`, `command:<name>`, `pre_gateway_dispatch`, reaction events, the event hook system)
capabilities.hermes: Plugins get an observation point before every recognised slash command and a veto/rewrite point (`command:<name>` can deny, mark handled, or rewrite). `pre_gateway_dispatch` lets a plugin drop, rewrite, or explicitly allow an inbound message — including from an unauthorized sender, bypassing pairing, for cases like a customer-handover ingest. Platform reactions are normalised and emitted to the hook registry. A general event hook system fires user handlers at gateway/agent lifecycle points. 5 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: No user-extensible lifecycle hooks. The only hook seams are kernel-owned: agents/core/kernel/binding.py:198 `make_egress_kernel_hook`, agents/core/http_client.py:56 `set_egress_kernel_hook`. `rg 'register_hook|fire_hook' agents/` → nothing.
capabilities.rationale: Worth having as the extensibility seam Nerva currently lacks — but copy it narrowed, and the narrowing is the point. Observation hooks (a plugin sees a command fired, a reaction landed) are safe and useful. Hermes's `pre_gateway_dispatch` explicitly lets a plugin admit an unauthorized sender and skip pairing; ported as-is that is a plugin-shaped hole straight through row 3's front door. In Nerva, deny and rewrite must stay with the kernel and the contract layer; a plugin may propose, never decide.
capabilities.governance: An inbound-rewrite hook is a privileged effect on the trust boundary — it changes what the agent believes the owner said. Register hooks through plugin_gate, audit every rewrite, and never let a hook grant authorization.

capabilities.name: Durable delivery ledger and dead-target registry (at-least-once replies)
capabilities.hermes: A durable row per outbound final response in `state.db` with three checkpoints around the send — `pending` before any attempt, `attempting` immediately before the await, `delivered`/`failed` after — plus owner-pid liveness. On startup, rows whose owning process died are claimed and redelivered; after an adapter reconnects without a restart, only an explicit allowlist of transient failures (`send_path_degraded`) may replay. Ambiguity is always labelled, never silently resent: `♻️ Recovered reply — the gateway restarted during delivery, so this may be a duplicate:`. Bounded by MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, 24 h freshness, 7-day retention, 500 rows. A dead-target registry remembers whole-chat `forbidden`/`not found` deaths and self-heals on the next success, deliberately not recording thread-level not-found. 3 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: none — `rg 'delivery_ledger|outbox|at.least.once' agents/` returns nothing. agents/core/channels/manager.py `send()` returns a bool that agents/core/orchestrator.py:1176 does not even check.
capabilities.rationale: This looks like plumbing and is actually an audit-integrity feature, which makes it more important for Nerva than for Hermes. Nerva's hash-chained log will faithfully record that an action was taken and a reply was produced; if the process dies before the platform confirms receipt, the owner never sees it and the log says otherwise. A governance product cannot have a silent gap between 'recorded' and 'delivered'. Copy the three-state design and, especially, the honest duplicate marker — labelling ambiguity instead of hiding it is exactly Nerva's posture.
capabilities.governance: Read-only with respect to the world, but it is the delivery half of the audit guarantee. Redelivery must not re-execute anything — it replays a stored message, never a re-run action.

capabilities.name: Restart, drain, crash forensics and process supervision
capabilities.hermes: Restart drains in-flight work then respawns through the supervisor or a detached child; affected sessions are notified and offered resume from the last committed turn; a one-shot 'the agent is back' message follows. A drain control marker lets an external process ask a running gateway to stop accepting new turns with no HTTP channel into it. Shutdown flush recovers messages and live transcripts that could not be written to state.db; shutdown forensics records who sent the SIGTERM; a lifecycle ledger records why the previous life ended including SIGKILL and kernel OOM. An in-process daemon thread probes the event loop and hard-exits with the service-restart code after N missed probes; systemd `Type=notify` + WatchdogSec heartbeats only while the loop makes progress. Restart-loop guard, respawn-storm backoff, code-skew detection ('restart the gateway' instead of a cryptic ImportError), cgroup cleanup of orphaned helpers, memory monitor, disk/memory status blocks, readiness probes, startup-restore queueing, a local control socket. ~26 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: agents/core/routers/ops.py:42 `/healthz`, :137 `/readyz`, :147 `/metrics`; scripts/runtime_supervisor.py; agents/core/observability/ (continuity_suite.py, reality_harness.py); agents/core/resilience.py. Missing entirely: drain, shutdown flush, lifecycle ledger, loop watchdog, code-skew, restart-loop guard. `rg 'watchdog|drain' agents/` → nothing.
capabilities.rationale: Copy the four that pay for themselves and leave the rest: **drain** (Nerva's channels live inside the FastAPI process, so a redeploy today interrupts live turns with no notice), **shutdown flush** (an unflushed transcript is lost evidence in a product whose transcript is evidence), the **lifecycle ledger** (docs/OWNER_TASKS.md says none of this has run on real hardware — 'why did it die' is precisely the question production will ask first), and the **loop watchdog** (an async hub driving cameras and a house can wedge, and only an out-of-loop thread can notice). Skip the local control socket: Nerva already has a loopback HTTP API with admin_guard, and a second unauthenticated local control plane is new attack surface for no new capability.
capabilities.governance: Restart and drain are privileged host operations. Triggered from chat they must cross `terminal.exec`-class mediation; triggered by the supervisor they are outside the agent's authority entirely and should stay that way.
capabilities.depends_on: per-session turn serialization (row 5) for a correct drain

capabilities.name: Platform adapter resilience (circuit breaker, pause/resume, reconnect backoff, connect timeout, credential/listener claims, token and connectivity guards)
capabilities.hermes: A failing adapter is isolated by a circuit breaker instead of taking the gateway down, and an operator can pause or resume an adapter live via `/platform list|pause|resume`. A reconnect watcher retries with exponential backoff and escalates a long-failing platform. `platform_connect_timeout` bounds a single `connect()`. Adapter/credential/listener claims stop two profiles polling the same bot token or binding the same port. Empty and obvious-placeholder tokens are refused at startup; 'connected' is a real predicate, not just 'enabled'. ~8 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: agents/core/resilience.py:132 `CircuitBreaker` and :223 `get_circuit_breaker` exist and are used — but only by plugins (agents/core/plugins/gmail_plugin.py, iot_control.py, cloud_llm.py …), never by a channel. agents/core/channels/manager.py `start_all` logs `E_CHANNEL_START_FAIL` and moves on; agents/core/channels/telegram.py:125 retries a failed poll with a bare 3 s sleep forever, with no backoff, no breaker and no escalation.
capabilities.rationale: The breaker Nerva needs is already written and tested — it is simply not wired to the one subsystem that talks to the outside world on a loop. A Telegram outage today means an unbounded tight retry with no signal to the owner; a revoked token means the same forever. Wire the existing breaker plus backoff into the adapters and add a `/platform` operator verb (row 25). The placeholder-token guard is a five-line addition that turns a silent dead channel into a startup error.
capabilities.governance: Read-only. Pausing or resuming an adapter from chat is operator control and belongs at the admin tier (row 2) with an audit entry.
capabilities.depends_on: per-command access tiers (row 2) for the `/platform` verb

capabilities.name: Multi-profile gateways, multiplexing, profile routes, relay, peer messaging, hosted rooms and cross-instance handoff
capabilities.hermes: One host can run many profiles as managed services, or opt into a multiplexer where the default profile's gateway serves every profile, with an allowlist; `profile_routes` splits guilds/channels/threads of a *shared* bot token across profiles; `room_link_url` publishes an HTTPS endpoint another gateway may call. Relay mode fronts platforms with an external connector that owns the credentials so the gateway holds no bot token, and can be made the exclusive ingress. `hermes peer` lets bots on one machine message bots on another. Hosted-room workers and a handoff watcher move sessions between instances. ~11 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: none — `rg 'multiplex|profile_routes|relay' agents/` returns nothing. agents/web.py:308 `lifespan` wires exactly one set of channels into one process.
capabilities.rationale: Two product reasons, not one. Multi-profile/multiplex/hosted-rooms solve a hosting-provider problem — many tenants on one box — and Nerva is one owner, one house, one hub; the whole shape would add a tenancy dimension to every session key, every audit row and every kernel decision for a user who does not exist. Relay is worse than merely unnecessary: it exists so an external connector holds the platform credentials instead of the gateway, which is the opposite of Nerva's local-first, loopback-only, own-your-keys posture, and docs/research/2026-09-06-hermes-and-field-gap-matrix.md already names cloud-fronted ingress as a non-goal. Re-open path: if a family or small-team mode ever ships, revisit profiles then — as scoped identities inside one kernel, never as parallel gateways.
capabilities.governance: read-only (nothing to build). Relay in particular would move credentials off the owner's machine, which no kernel kind can compensate for.

capabilities.name: Browser-control broker and artifact store
capabilities.hermes: An identity-scoped broker connects whoever physically drives a browser to callers talking to it over any transport, without the broker knowing anything about HTTP or WebSocket; a one-shot authenticated HTTPS upload/download path moves bounded browser-control artifacts. 2 entries.

capabilities.name: Scale-to-zero (idle self-suspend of the host)
capabilities.hermes: After `gateway.scale_to_zero.idle_timeout_minutes` of inbound quiet the gateway quiesces its relay link and suspends its own machine. 2 entries.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: none — `rg 'scale_to_zero|idle_timeout' agents/` returns nothing.
capabilities.rationale: This is a hosted-deployment cost feature: it exists so a relay-fronted gateway stops billing VM-hours between messages. Nerva's box is not billed by the hour and is not idle — it runs camera ingestion (agents/core/routers/cameras.py start_camera_ingestion), presence, heartbeats and the night lane of company mode, all of which suspending would silently kill. Shipping it would trade the always-on house brain for a saving the owner does not pay. Re-open path: a laptop-only 'travel profile' with no house role, where suspending is correct behaviour rather than a regression.
capabilities.governance: read-only (nothing to build)

capabilities.name: Gateway configuration surface (layered load order, per-platform shared keys, env overrides, platform enum, port-binding conflicts, cwd/SSL/venv bootstraps)
capabilities.hermes: `load_gateway_config()` merges four layers lowest→highest: dataclass defaults → legacy `gateway.json` → `config.yaml` (with administrator pins applied first) → environment, then validates; a malformed config.yaml logs and continues on the lower layers. Every top-level key is also accepted nested under `gateway:`, with 'key present, not key truthy' precedence. A shared-key loop copies ~30 behaviour keys into each platform's `extra` regardless of nesting; an open enum admits plugin platforms only from bundled dirs or a registry, rejecting arbitrary strings; a single `platform_binds_port` predicate is consulted by both startup validation and the dashboard's pre-write validation so policy cannot drift. ~14 entries incl. the cwd placeholder, Windows venv and SSL bootstraps.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: agents/core/settings_db.py is the live settings store the /admin HUD writes and the orchestrator watches (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:340 re-reads it live); agents/core/env_config.py and agents/core/config.py carry env and defaults; docs/FLAGS.md is a per-flag ledger of default, effect, cost and revert story that Hermes has no equivalent of.
capabilities.rationale: Nerva's single settings DB plus a flags document with an explicit revert story is a better shape than a four-layer YAML/JSON/env merge whose own rebuild note admits it needs a provenance map. Keep it. The one idea worth borrowing is that rebuild note: emit which layer set each effective value, so 'why is this on' has an answer without reading code — cheap, and it fits Nerva's audit posture.
capabilities.governance: read-only

capabilities.name: The gateway process model itself (one always-on process owning adapters, sessions and the cron tick; the ordered inbound pipeline)
capabilities.hermes: `hermes gateway` runs one long-lived asyncio process that connects every enabled adapter, owns the per-chat session store, runs a 60 s cron tick and dispatches to `AIAgent`; it installs as a systemd user unit or launchd plist, writes pid/lock/state files under `$HERMES_HOME`, and exits 75 to ask for a restart or 78 to mark a permanent config failure so the supervisor stops respawning. The inbound pipeline is an ordered gauntlet every message passes before it can become a turn. ~9 entries incl. the docs pages and package API.
capabilities.nerva_evidence: agents/web.py:308 `lifespan` is Nerva's equivalent: it enforces boot posture, scaffolds the data home, builds the Orchestrator, constructs the Gateway (web.py:339) and registers web/voice/telegram/discord/email/slack plus configured webhook channels, then starts channels and camera ingestion in one FastAPI process. agents/core/channels/gateway.py:57 `route()` is the inbound gauntlet (rate limit → pairing → taint marking via security/taint + detect_injection → inbox record → handler).
capabilities.rationale: One process is the right call for a single-owner hub, and folding the gateway into the same process as the HUD API removes a whole class of IPC and lock problems Hermes has to solve (control socket, pid/lock, code skew). Nerva's gauntlet is also doing something Hermes's is not — marking untrusted inbound as tainted and scanning for injection before the handler sees it. The honest cost to record: channel availability is now coupled to the API process, which is why the drain and loop-watchdog items in row 23 matter more here than they would in a separate-process design.
capabilities.governance: The pipeline is the trust boundary — taint marking here is what lets the kernel later force a plan derived from inbound text back to ASK.
